text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
AL-AHRAM
- Iraqi developments

- Foreign Minister Amr Moussa, after talks with the foreign minister of Norway, says: "The Iraqi people must not be punished. We must work to rescue them. Israel must withdraw from Hebron and stop expanding settlements."

- The ministerial group for cotton, in its meeting yesterday under Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri, decided that the Principal Bank for Credit and Agricultural Development will take delivery of all cotton which farmers want to deliver to it and will pay the price immediately, at a minimum of 500 pounds a qantar (50 kg), despite the fall in world prices.
- Ibrahim Nafie in front-page editorial: "A question to the British: You fight terrorism and then host the biggest terrorist gathering. How?"
- Palestinian President Yasser Arafat will arrive in Egypt tomorrow, meet Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak and brief him on his talks with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
AL-AKHBAR
- Iraqi developments. Turkish forces mass on border.
- Universities are accepting 265,000 students this year, 34,000 more than last year.

- It has been decided to implement 10 Egyptian-Kuwaiti investment projects with a capital of 15 billion pounds ($4.4 billion). The projects will be promoted during an official visit to Kuwait on September 14 by a group of ministers. It has also been decided to lift all restrictions on exporting cotton, as long as farmers are paid at least 500 pounds a qantar.
- Yesterday the Registrar's Office started to implement the cabinet's decision to reduce its fees.
AL-GOMHURIA

- Oil Minister Hamdi el-Banbi says new oil discoveries will soon be announced from the Mediterranean and the Gulf of Suez. Banbi was opening expansion work at Amreyah Petroleum Refining. He said the petroleum sector is now carrying out projects costing 220 million pounds.
- Medical college admission requires 92.8 percent in new secondary school exams, 95 percent in old ones. Engineeriung requires 86.5 percent (new) or 92.2 percent (old).
- Twelve customs officials from Damietta are being questioned by the investigating magistrate. They deprived the state of 100 million pounds in revenue.
AL-WAFD

- In the next few days Ganzouri will discuss the draft laws on companies, investment, dumping and monopolies. He will try to sort out the disagreements between the ministries of economy, supply and finance and the General Authority for Investment.
$1 = 3.40 pounds
